CVE-2026-111070.title: Content Pilot <= 2.2.4 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via RSS-linked article `<meta name="description">`
CVE-2026-111070.description: The Content Pilot – Autoblogging & Affiliate Marketing Suite plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 2.2.4. This is due to the plugin extracting the HTML meta description from each remotely-fetched article (WPCP_Readability::parse_meta()), piping that value through the article template substitution and html_entity_decode() in WPCP_Module::insert_post(), and then calling wp_insert_post() after switching the current user to the configured campaign author (an Administrator with the unfiltered_html capability by default) — so no wp_kses_post sanitization is applied to the attacker-controlled HTML before it is persisted as post_content and rendered on the front end. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers who control the content of any RSS source an administrator has configured a Content Pilot RSS campaign to consume to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

CVE-2026-116570.title: FreeSWITCH: Pre-authentication stack buffer overflow in mod_xml_rpc HTTP directory authentication
CVE-2026-116570.description: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. Prior to 1.11.2, http_directory_auth() rebuilt an expected user@domain:password credential and base64-encoded it into an 80-byte buffer using an encoder without an output-length argument. A configured credential longer than 57 characters overflowed the stack before the supplied HTTP Basic password was compared. An unauthenticated client only needed to name an existing directory user on an exposed mod_xml_rpc HTTP listener; the module is built but not loaded by the stock configuration. The overflow can corrupt the stack and crash FreeSWITCH, ending every active call, although the overrun bytes come from the configured credential and remote code execution has not been demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.2.

CVE-2026-121745.title: nvm exposes NVM_AUTH_HEADER to other local users on the curl/wget command line
CVE-2026-121745.description: Node Version Manager (nvm) is a POSIX-compliant shell function for managing multiple node.js versions. In versions 0.40.0 through 0.40.8, when `NVM_AUTH_HEADER` is set, `nvm_download` passes the credential to curl or wget as a `--header "Authorization: ..."` command-line argument. Process arguments are visible to every local user (on Linux via `ps` or `/proc//cmdline` unless `/proc` is mounted with `hidepid=`; on macOS via `ps`), so another unprivileged account on the same machine can read the token while nvm is downloading during `nvm ls-remote`, `nvm install`, and similar commands, and gain whatever access it grants on the private mirror. Only users who set `NVM_AUTH_HEADER` on a host shared with other local accounts are affected. Version 0.41.0 passes the header to curl on stdin and to GNU Wget in a private temporary config file. BusyBox wget reads no config file, so when it is the only downloader available the header is still passed as an argument.

CVE-2026-77299.title: Regexp2: Unbounded memory amplification via large `{m}` quantifier on a zero-width subexpression
CVE-2026-77299.description: Regexp2 is a feature-rich RegExp engine for Go. Prior to version 2.3.0, when regexp2 compiles and matches a pattern containing a large fixed-count quantifier applied to a zero-width subexpression — e.g. (?:){50000000} — the match engine executes the empty loop body m-1 times, pushing two integers onto the backtracking stack on every iteration. Because the parser accepts any repetition count up to math.MaxInt32 and the backtracking stack grows without bound, a pattern of fewer than 20 bytes matched against an empty input can force multi-gigabyte allocation and OOM-kill the process. MatchTimeout does not fully mitigate this because the memory is allocated faster than the 100 ms timeout clock can fire. This issue has been patched in version 2.3.0.

CVE-2026-99512.title: media: au0828: fix use-after-free in bulk_timeout timer on disconnect
CVE-2026-99512.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

media: au0828: fix use-after-free in bulk_timeout timer on disconnect

start_urb_transfer() arms dev->bulk_timeout, whose callback
au0828_bulk_timeout() queues dev->restart_streaming; that work in turn
calls start_urb_transfer() and re-arms the timer.

au0828_dvb_unregister() cancels restart_streaming on disconnect but does
not sync bulk_timeout. au0828_usb_release() then frees dev with kfree(),
so a timer still armed or pending at that point can fire after the free
and dereference dev through timer_container_of().

Sync the timer with timer_shutdown_sync() before cancel_work_sync(). The
timer callback queues the work, so the timer must be stopped first; the
shutdown variant is needed because the work re-arms the timer through
start_urb_transfer(). The dvb->frontend == NULL early return guards the
register-failure path where the timer was never set up.

This bug was found by static analysis.

CVE-2026-99794.title: Bluetooth: L2CAP: Reject signalling responses in invalid states
CVE-2026-99794.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: L2CAP: Reject signalling responses in invalid states

A peer can send configuration messages while an
incoming channel is in BT_CONNECT2, before the
security or deferred accept gate has completed. A
configuration response can then promote the channel
to BT_CONNECTED. Configuration responses can also
act on channels that are closing, and a late connection
response can move a disconnecting channel back to
BT_CONFIG.

Accept connection responses only while waiting in
BT_CONNECT. Answer configuration requests in
BT_CONNECT2, but defer our own request until
BT_CONFIG so configuration cannot complete before
the gate. Ignore configuration responses outside
BT_CONFIG and BT_CONNECTED, and only complete
configuration in BT_CONFIG.
